newsitem.title: USA: Saudis offer data to U.S. on bombing - report.
newsitem.headline: Saudis offer data to U.S. on bombing - report.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has given the United States detailed data to support the Saudis' belief that the bombing of a U.S. military complex was carried out by Shiite extremists trained in Lebanon and backed by Iran, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper said the Saudi interior minister in charge of security, Prince Nayef, handed the evidence to FBI Director Louis Freeh during Freeh's visit to Riyadh last month.

The data included confessions extracted from some of 40 Saudi Shiites detained and accused of involvement in the June 25 bombing that killed 19 U.S. servicemen at the Khobar Towers housing complex in Dhahran.

In addition, the material contained results of Saudi wiretaps and other electronic eavesdropping and a detailed account of the movements of key alleged conspirators into and out of Saudi Arabia, Lebanon's Bekaa Valley, Damascus and Tehran, it said.

The newspaper said senior Saudi officials had suggested to the Clinton administration that the United States could lead other nations in taking some form of military and diplomatic action against Iran early next year if the United States agreed that Tehran was linked to the bombing.

ABC-TV reported on Friday that Saudi officials had shown Freeh videotaped confessions of six accused men who also provided information about links between Iran and extremists who carried out the bombing.

The six men said they were recruited by an Iranian intelligence agent while at a religious celebration in Damascus, Syria. They said they received "religious training" over the next 18 months in Iran's holy city of Gom, and spent time at two Hezbollah guerrilla training camps in Syria and Lebanon, ABC said.
The FBI declined to comment on either report.

Law enforcement officials previously had complained about a lack of co-operation from Saudi authorities in the investigation. They said FBI agents were not allowed to question Saudi citizens and were not told about any arrests.
Defense Secretary William Perry told reporters last month the United States had not yet concluded who was responsible for the bombing.
